lessons.title: Present perfect or simple past?
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)
objectives: Choose between the present perfect and the simple past using the time marker.
Form the present perfect with have/has + past participle.
Avoid the French-influenced mistake « I have seen him yesterday ».

blocks.title: Two tenses, two points of view
blocks.md:
**Simple past** (*I saw*, *she went*): a **finished** action at a **finished time** (yesterday, last year, in 2019, two days ago).

**Present perfect** (*have / has + past participle*: *I have seen*, *she has gone*): a link with **now**: an experience, a recent action with a result now, or a situation that **continues** up to now.

*Astuce* : en français on dit « J'ai mangé hier » ; en anglais, avec *yesterday*, on dit **I ate** yesterday.

blocks.caption: Past simple: a point or a period that is finished. Present perfect: from the past up to now.
blocks.alt: A time line going from past to now. Under the past part, a short mark labelled simple past: last Monday. Above, an arrow from the past reaching now, labelled present perfect: since 2020.

items.text: Simple past = finished time. Present perfect = link with now.

blocks.title: Time markers
blocks.md:
- **Present perfect**: *already, yet, just, ever, never, so far, recently*; *since* + starting point (since 2018); *for* + duration (for three years).
- **Simple past**: *yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago, when I was ten*.

With *ago* or a finished date, never use the present perfect.

blocks.title: Form and irregular verbs
blocks.md:
- Affirmative: *She has finished.* Negative: *She hasn't finished.* Question: *Has she finished?*
- Irregular verbs (infinitive - past - participle): go - went - gone; see - saw - seen; write - wrote - written; eat - ate - eaten; take - took - taken; do - did - done; begin - began - begun; swim - swam - swum; buy - bought - bought.

blocks.title: Example 1: put the verbs in the correct tense
blocks.statement: Complete: *I ___ (visit) Kribi last August, but I ___ (not / swim) in the sea yet.*

steps.md: First gap: *last August* is a finished time, so we use the **simple past**: *visited*.
Second gap: *yet* shows that the action may still happen, a link with now, so we use the **present perfect** negative: *haven't swum*.

blocks.answer: **I visited Kribi last August, but I haven't swum in the sea yet.**

blocks.title: Example 2: correct the mistakes
blocks.statement: Correct each sentence: (a) *I have seen him yesterday.* (b) *She lived here since 2018.*

steps.md: (a) *yesterday* is a finished time: **I saw him yesterday.**
(b) *since 2018* means she still lives here: **She has lived here since 2018.**

blocks.answer: (a) I saw him yesterday. (b) She has lived here since 2018.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- *I have seen him yesterday.* (finished time + present perfect)
- *She has went* (use the participle: *has gone*).
- Translating the French passé composé word for word: the English tense depends on the time marker, not on the French sentence.
- *since* with a duration or *for* with a starting point: *for three years*, *since 2020*.

items: Make a list of ten irregular verbs and learn the three forms.
Tell a friend what you have done this week and what you did last weekend.

exercises.explanation: *Last Saturday* is a finished time: simple past, *won*.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: Ebene ___ a lion in his life.
exercises.explanation: No finished time is given and the sentence speaks about a life experience: present perfect. The subject *Ebene* is singular, so *has*, followed by the participle *seen*.
exercises.method: Singular subject: has. Then the participle.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: True or false: « I have finished my homework two hours ago. » is correct.
exercises.explanation: False. *Two hours ago* is a finished time: **I finished my homework two hours ago.**
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with the reason for the tense.
pairs: I lost my keys, so I can't open the door.
I lost my keys on Monday.
situation that continues up to now
I lived there for two years and then I left.
exercises.explanation: The first sentence has a result now; the second names a finished day; the third uses *since*; the fourth is a finished period.
exercises.method: Ask: finished time or link with now?
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: Put the verbs in brackets in the correct tense: *Tabi ___ (teach) at this school since 2016. Last year he ___ (win) a prize.*
exercises.model: Tabi **has taught** at this school since 2016. Last year he **won** a prize.
exercises.explanation: *Since 2016* continues up to now: present perfect. *Last year* is finished: simple past.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: Write four sentences about yourself: two with the **present perfect** (things you have done) and two with the **simple past** (with a finished time).
exercises.model: I have visited Yaoundé twice. I have never eaten pineapple jam. Last Sunday I played football with my cousins. I went to church two days ago.
rubric: 1 mark each correct sentence: correct tense for its marker, correct verb form, correct spelling. Accept any correct personal sentences.
exercises.explanation: A good answer uses *have/has + participle* for the first two and a finished time (last Sunday, ago, in 2022) for the last two.
exercises.method: Do not use *ago* or *yesterday* with the present perfect.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

choices: She has gone to the market yesterday.
She went to the market yesterday.
She has went to the market yesterday.
She goes to the market yesterday.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: What is the past participle of *write*?
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: I ___ my phone and I can't find it.
exercises.explanation: A recent action with a result now: *have lost*.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: Which time expression goes with the present perfect?
exercises.explanation: *Since Monday* links the past to now.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.explanation: *Ever* in a question about experience: *Have you ever eaten...?*
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)

exercises.prompt: Write a short letter (about 70 words) to a friend. Tell him or her two things you have done this month, one thing you did last weekend, and what you would do if you had a free holiday.
exercises.model:
Dear Ngo,
How are you? This month I have started a reading club and I have finished my first English book. Last weekend I visited my grandmother in the village. If I had a free holiday, I would travel to the coast and swim in the sea.
Write soon.
Your friend, Paul
rubric: 2 marks: content (all four points are covered).
2 marks: grammar (present perfect, simple past, type 2 conditional).
2 marks: layout of a letter (greeting, paragraphs, closing) and spelling.
exercises.explanation: The letter must use the present perfect, the simple past with a finished time, and a type 2 conditional.
exercises.method: Plan the four points before you write.
exercises.source: Original exercise, BEPC style (to be reviewed by a teacher)
